content.title: Cornyn reconsiders Senate filibuster as he and Paxton stay in runoff race
content.text: WASHINGTON — When former President Joe Biden pushed to change the Senate’s filibuster rule that requires a 60-vote majority in order to pass voting rights legislation, it prompted criticism from the senior senator from Texas. What You Need To Know After years of defending the Senate’s filibuster rules, Texas Republican U.S. Sen. John Cornyn is now signaling he may be open to reforms The comments come amid a partial government shutdown affecting the Department of Homeland Security and President Donald Trump's push to pass the SAVE America Act, which would require Americans to provide proof of U.S. citizenship when voting in federal elections Cornyn and Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton will both remain on the May 26 runoff ballot as an endorsement from Trump looms “I oppose any effort to eliminate or weaken the legislative filibuster,” Sen. John Cornyn said in January 2022. But now, Cornyn is open to some procedural changes. This comes as Congress has failed to fund the Department of Homeland Security. The partial government shutdown has led to long lines at airports in Texas and across the country. Republicans like Cornyn have rejected Democrats’ requests to separate funding for the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) from immigration enforcement operations. Some Democrats are calling for a major overhaul of U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) as well as U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) under the Trump administration. “These folks have now gone without pay for two pay periods. They are not wealthy people, and so many of them are having to decide whether to pay the rent or put food on the table, and that’s just unacceptable,” Cornyn said. “If you fund the Department of Homeland Security, then we can have the conversations about what sort of reforms may be necessary, but not while holding these TSA agents hostage.” President Donald Trump is also pushing for the passage of what is known as the SAVE America Act. The legislation would require Americans to provide proof of U.S. citizenship when voting in federal elections. Four years ago, Cornyn said regarding the filibuster, “There’s no scenario in which partisan wins are more important than the long term stability for our laws and our public policy.” When asked what makes the SAVE America Act and funding DHS different today, Cornyn told Spectrum News, “Well, we’ve never had this sort of polarization before.” “There is nothing more important than making sure that the vote, the ballot is cast by only those qualified to vote,” Cornyn continued. That’s the very foundation of our government, consent of the governed, and that’s how that consent is manifested. So that’s caused me to reconsider something called the talking filibuster, which I am happy to support, and then if there are other reforms necessary to get some of these most basic measures passed, I’d be open to that conversation.” Cornyn is currently seeking reelection. He finished first in the March 3 primary but did not capture the majority needed to avoid a runoff against Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton. In a statement, Paxton said in part, “Only after I called him out repeatedly did he flip-flop—once again proving he only does the right thing when it’s in his best interest. If John Cornyn had cared as much about helping President Trump pass the Save America Act as he did helping Corrupt Biden push gun control, this would already be law. If the Save America Act fails, it will be because John Cornyn refused to truly fight to get it done. He’s campaigned on being Mr. Effective in the Swamp, and it’s time for him to put his money where his mouth is.” When asked to comment on how Paxton suggested he pushed Cornyn in this direction, Cornyn said, “He’s proven himself to be untrustworthy, and I think this is just another example. He says all sorts of things, including to his own family, that aren’t true. He’s lied to taxpayers, he’s lied to his own senior staff, and I don’t think he’s a credible person, so I don’t really pay much attention to what he says, because you can’t trust him.” Trump has indicated his endorsement in the runoff may hinge on the SAVE America Act. “I talked to the President on a regular basis. I know how important the SAVE America Act is to him. I support it, and I’m going to do everything I can to see that it’s passed into the law,” Cornyn said. “If he decides to make an endorsement along the way, I would certainly welcome that, but we’re not waiting around for that to happen, because we’ve got work to do.” Tuesday marked the deadline for candidates to get off the runoff ballot, and it appears the names of both Republican candidates will be on the ballot for the May 26 election. Cornyn also said he would be “more than happy” to have a debate with Paxton. “I would be surprised if he accepts because he’s done everything he can to avoid answering hard questions,” Cornyn said.
